[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard mandates that an autonomous agent dispatch pipeline **never redundantly executes work that has already shipped**, and that when it encounters an already-satisfied deliverable it **no-ops with provenance** rather than duplicating or improvising. It defines three control points — a **pre-dispatch idempotency gate**, an **agent no-op-with-provenance** contract, and **duplicate-cluster collapse** at reconcile — all keyed on the universal deliverable **stable-ID** (STD-GOV-AI-003). It is the mandatory realization of [ADR-GOV-012](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-012-forward-only-change-propagation-and-execution-idempotency.md).
page_texts.5:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#scope]

### Scope

**Covered:** the three idempotency control points; the stable-ID as the deduplication key; the `@unresolved` provenance-anchor honesty rule; and the interaction with forward-only change propagation.

**Not covered:** the stable-ID / Built-From format itself (STD-GOV-AI-003); the label taxonomy (STD-GOV-AI-002); the general execution model (ADR-GOV-009); how a *spec* change is authored (that is the governed modify front doors and forward-only emission, ADR-GOV-012 / ADR-GOV-011).
page_texts.6:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

**Mandatory.** An agent dispatch pipeline that can redundantly execute an already-shipped deliverable, or whose agent improvises on already-built work, is non-compliant.
page_texts.7:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

Autonomous agents run in parallel and continuously; without an idempotency contract they duplicate already-shipped work (direct cost) and produce non-deterministic "complete-with-no-PR" records (audit-trail corruption). On one exemplar project the absence of these controls produced ~45 redundant agent executions and ~30 corrupt completion records. Because the record of *what was built* is HIPAA/CMS audit evidence, deterministic, idempotent execution is a governance requirement, not merely an efficiency one.
page_texts.9:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

- **REQ-001 — Pre-dispatch idempotency gate.** Before dispatching any agent, the pipeline MUST resolve the incoming work item's deliverable **stable-ID** (STD-GOV-AI-003) and query for a sibling with the **same** stable-ID that is already shipped (closed-completed with resolved provenance). If one exists, the pipeline MUST NOT dispatch; it MUST apply `agent:duplicate` (STD-GOV-AI-002), comment `superseded by #<canonical>`, and close the incoming item as not-planned.
- **REQ-002 — No-op-with-provenance contract.** An agent that determines its named deliverable is **already fully built** MUST no-op, citing the canonical artifact/PR as provenance, rather than re-implementing or improvising. A **partial** deliverable proceeds normally; genuine **ambiguity** MUST halt to loopback rather than guess. (This supersedes any "never no-op" instruction.)
- **REQ-003 — Duplicate-cluster collapse at reconcile.** A reconcile pass MUST group work items by **full** stable-ID, keep the canonical member (closed-completed with resolved provenance), and close the rest as duplicates. A genuine multi-layer / multi-screen deliverable (distinct stable-IDs, >1 resolved member) MUST NOT be collapsed.
- **REQ-004 — Full stable-ID keying.** All three controls MUST key on the **full** stable-ID (e.g. `<concern>-<feature-slug>[-<layer>]`), never a truncated prefix, so distinct layers/screens of one contract are never wrongly treated as duplicates.
- **REQ-005 — Provenance-anchor honesty (`@unresolved`).** When a shipped item's merge commit is genuinely unrecoverable, the pipeline MUST record an explicit `@unresolved` provenance anchor rather than fabricating one. A guessed anchor corrupts idempotency and drift detection and is prohibited.
page_texts.10:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

- Compute the stable-ID deterministically from the governing spec identity so it is stable across re-runs.
- Emit an audit log entry for every no-op and every duplicate-collapse, citing the canonical item.
- Run the pre-dispatch gate as part of the same Stage-1 validation that checks routing and traceability.
page_texts.11:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

- **Redundant dispatch.** Dispatching an agent for a deliverable whose stable-ID already shipped is prohibited (REQ-001).
- **Improvise-on-built.** An agent re-implementing or inventing work when its deliverable already exists is prohibited (REQ-002).
- **Prefix collapse.** Deduplicating on a truncated stable-ID (collapsing distinct layers/screens) is prohibited (REQ-004).
- **Fabricated provenance.** Guessing a merge-commit anchor instead of recording `@unresolved` is prohibited (REQ-005).
page_texts.12:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

1. Submit to the Governance EA Lead: the pipeline, the control that cannot be met, and interim risk acceptance.
2. Approval authority: Governance EA Lead; ARB where audit-trail integrity is affected.
3. Document the exception, expiry, and remediation.
4. Review each release until remediated.
page_texts.15:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#the-three-control-points]

#### The three control points

| Control | When | Input | Action on match |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pre-dispatch gate (REQ-001) | Stage 1, before dispatch | incoming stable-ID | skip + `agent:duplicate` + comment + close-not-planned |
| No-op-with-provenance (REQ-002) | agent runtime | the deliverable's build state | no-op citing canonical PR (fully built); proceed (partial); halt-loopback (ambiguous) |
| Duplicate-cluster collapse (REQ-003) | reconcile | all items grouped by full stable-ID | keep canonical, close rest as duplicates |
page_texts.16:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#canonical-match-definition]

#### Canonical-match definition

A sibling is the **canonical shipped** deliverable for a stable-ID when it is closed as completed **and** carries a resolved provenance anchor (a Built-From merge-commit SHA, not `@unresolved`). Matching MUST use the full stable-ID.
page_texts.17:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#architecture-constraints]

### Architecture Constraints

- **Constraint 1 — Depends on stable-ID + Built-From.** These controls require the universal stable-ID and Built-From/Supersedes chain (STD-GOV-AI-003); a pipeline lacking them cannot be compliant with this standard.
- **Constraint 2 — Forward-only interaction.** A post-go-live *change* is not a duplicate — it is a new superseding item with a new/other stable-ID facet per forward-only propagation (ADR-GOV-012); the gate MUST distinguish "same deliverable already shipped" from "superseding change".
page_texts.18:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#technology-standards]

### Technology Standards

_Technology-agnostic; applies to any issue-tracker-driven agent dispatch pipeline (e.g. gh-aw, per GUID-TECH-IMPL-004)._
page_texts.20:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#idempotency-signal-pipeline-stage-1-output]

#### Idempotency signal (pipeline Stage 1 output)

```json
{
  "stable_id": "claims-adjudicate-service",
  "canonical": "1234",          // sibling issue # already shipped for this stable-id, or "" if none
  "provenance": "@a1b2c3d4"     // resolved merge anchor, or "@unresolved"
}
```
page_texts.23:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#phase-1-wire-the-pre-dispatch-gate]

#### Phase 1: Wire the pre-dispatch gate

1. Resolve the incoming item's full stable-ID.
2. Query closed-completed siblings sharing that stable-ID with resolved provenance.
3. On match: `agent:duplicate`, comment, close-not-planned; on no match: proceed.
page_texts.24:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#phase-2-agent-contract--reconcile]

#### Phase 2: Agent contract + reconcile

1. Give the agent the canonical-build signal so it can no-op with provenance (REQ-002).
2. Add a reconcile pass that collapses duplicate clusters by full stable-ID (REQ-003).
page_texts.25:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#validation-criteria]

### Validation Criteria

| Validation Area | Criteria | Verification Method | Evidence Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pre-dispatch gate | already-shipped stable-ID is not re-dispatched | dispatch-log review | skip + `agent:duplicate` record |
| No-op contract | agent no-ops on fully-built deliverable | agent-run log | no-op-with-provenance entry |
| Cluster collapse | reconcile keeps canonical, closes duplicates | reconcile report | grouped-by-stable-ID output |
| Full-ID keying | distinct layers not collapsed | review | stable-ID granularity check |
page_texts.26:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#testing-requirements]

### Testing Requirements

- **Idempotency Testing**: dispatching a shipped stable-ID twice yields exactly one build and one skip.
- **No-op Testing**: an agent handed an already-built deliverable produces a no-op-with-provenance, not a PR.
- **Compliance Testing**: reconcile on a seeded duplicate set collapses to the canonical member without collapsing distinct layers.
page_texts.27:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#documentation-requirements]

### Documentation Requirements

- The dispatch/no-op/reconcile audit logs.
- The stable-ID → canonical mapping produced at Stage 1.
page_texts.30:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#assessment-criteria]

#### Assessment Criteria

- No redundant dispatch for already-shipped stable-IDs.
- No agent improvisation on already-built deliverables.
- Reconcile collapses only true duplicates.
page_texts.31:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#assessment-process]

#### Assessment Process

1. Review dispatch and reconcile logs for a sample period.
2. Confirm every no-op cites a canonical PR.
3. Report violations as release-gating remediation.
page_texts.32:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#monitoring-requirements]

### Monitoring Requirements

- **Continuous Monitoring**: dispatch/no-op/collapse events logged and auditable.
- **Periodic Reviews**: idempotency metrics (redundant dispatches = 0) reviewed each release.
- **Incident Reporting**: a redundant execution or corrupt completion record opens a remediation item.
page_texts.33:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#exception-handling]

### Exception Handling

Temporary (stable-ID/Built-From not yet available), permanent (rare; ARB where audit integrity is affected), emergency waivers per the [Exceptions Process](#exceptions-process), with expiry and review.
page_texts.34:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#governance-oversight]

### Governance Oversight

- **Standards Owner**: Governance EA Lead (AI Development).
- **Compliance Manager**: monitors idempotency metrics and audit-trail integrity.
- **Governance Body**: ARB for audit-trail-affecting exceptions.
- **Subject Matter Experts**: Platform Engineering (pipeline), Technology EA Lead (dispatch substrate).
page_texts.37:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#example-1-pre-dispatch-skip]

#### Example 1: Pre-dispatch skip

**Context:** an issue re-created for `claims-adjudicate-service`, already shipped under #1234.
**Implementation:** Stage 1 resolved the stable-ID, matched #1234 (closed-completed, resolved anchor), applied `agent:duplicate`, commented `superseded by #1234`, closed not-planned — no agent ran.
**Compliance Evidence:** dispatch log skip entry.
**Lessons Learned:** the gate prevented a redundant run before any cost was incurred.
page_texts.38:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-004-agent-execution-idempotency-standard.md#example-2-distinct-layers-not-collapsed]

#### Example 2: Distinct layers not collapsed

**Context:** `enrollment-ui-000` (foundation) and `enrollment-ui-001` (screen) share a feature but have distinct full stable-IDs.
**Implementation:** reconcile grouped by full stable-ID and kept both — they are not duplicates.
**Compliance Evidence:** reconcile report showing two retained canonicals.
**Lessons Learned:** full-ID keying (REQ-004) is what prevents wrongful collapse.
